correctness.rationale: The signed derivative has zero mass; its Jordan positive/negative parts give an exact barycentric representation by arc derivatives. Hilbert strict convexity and injectivity of I-H_t modulo constants prove every equality case. Fourier normalization accounts for both signs and two jumps, giving E_t(d) with coefficient 1/(2 pi^2). A Gaussian overlap bound uniform for 0<=d<=1/2 controls all circle-periodization cross terms by C sqrt(t) exp(-1/(32t)). The exact line Fourier scaling gives F(d/(2 sqrt(t))); its derivative is (2 erfc(z)-erfc(z/sqrt(2)))/2. Strictly increasing Gaussian hazard yields a unique maximum with a smaller limit at infinity, proving convergence of every maximizing d_t and the leading constant. The locally extracted checker passed 52 finite assertions, but proofs of infinite statements are analytical.

value.rationale: The sharp Gaussian heat BV-to-L2 error is a canonical operator norm relevant to smoothing discontinuities. The theorem exactly identifies its extremal geometry and microscopic interaction: two jumps separate by 2 z_* sqrt(t), producing a 20.01 percent larger squared error than every fixed positive jump separation. The limiting coefficient/root and all-time arc rigidity are structurally motivated, not arbitrary parameter slices, and no downstream application is needed to make the exact benchmark valuable.
